title: Portfolio
subtitle: Legal drafting, litigation, HR, research and organisational work, each told as a short case study: the situation, my role, what I did and what it delivered.

items.title: Leading 50+ Bank Indonesia Scholarship Awardees Across 20 Community Development Projects at GenBI UPN Veteran Jawa Timur
items.organization: GenBI UPN Veteran Jawa Timur Commissariat
items.summary: Directing strategy, team coordination and programme evaluation across education, environment, English communication and entrepreneurship projects.
situation: GenBI is the Bank Indonesia scholarship community, and each commissariat is expected to give back through community programmes. At UPN Veteran Jawa Timur, projects were running in parallel with little shared planning.
With a large membership and a short leadership term, the commissariat needed a clear strategy, an evaluation habit and a way to keep every project owner accountable.
items.task: As President, I set the organisation's direction and was accountable for coordination across all teams and for evaluating the programmes they ran.

steps.title: Set the strategy
steps.description: Defined priority themes for the term: education, environmental sustainability, capacity-building, English communication and entrepreneurship.

steps.title: Organise the teams
steps.description: Assigned project leads, agreed on timelines and set a regular rhythm of progress meetings.

steps.title: Evaluate and improve
steps.description: Introduced a short evaluation after each programme so lessons carried into the next one.

resultNotes: Twenty community development projects planned and tracked under one strategy.
Programme evaluation became a standing step rather than an afterthought.

items.title: Company Regulations, Agreements and Demand Letters
items.summary: Drafted and reviewed company regulations, PKWT and PKWTT agreements, cooperation agreements, lawsuits and demand letters (somasi) for client businesses.

metrics.label: Chapters in a company regulation draft

situation: Client companies needed employment documents that matched current labour regulation. Several relied on old templates that no longer fitted their workforce or their working arrangements.
At the same time, new businesses needed their registrations and licences in order, including NPWP registration and OSS licensing, before they could start hiring.
items.task: As Legal Staff, I assisted the attorneys with drafting and reviewing employment and corporate documents, and with the legal research behind them.

steps.title: Research the rules
steps.description: Checked the relevant labour, corporate and environmental regulations before each draft, and noted the clauses that mattered most to the client.

steps.title: Draft the documents
steps.description: Prepared company regulations, PKWT and PKWTT agreements, collective labour agreements, MoUs and NDAs from the client's facts.

steps.title: Review and revise
steps.description: Reviewed drafts against checklists, tracked comments from supervising attorneys and delivered clean final versions.

resultNotes: Clients received documents consistent with current employment regulation.
Supported several businesses through NPWP registration and OSS licensing.
Sample documents shown here use fictional company names.

items.title: Court Hearings and Legal Research at Bapas and HHL
items.role: Legal Research Intern, then Legal Staff
items.organization: Balai Pemasyarakatan Kelas IA Surabaya & HHL Associates Attorney At Law
items.summary: Researched criminal justice regulations at Bapas Surabaya, prepared civil pleadings at HHL Associates, and attended hearings and mediation in tort, breach of contract and marriage cases.

metrics.label: Placements: Bapas and a law firm

situation: My first placement was at Balai Pemasyarakatan (Bapas) Kelas IA Surabaya, the correctional centre that supports the criminal justice process. A year later I joined HHL Associates, a law firm handling civil and corporate matters.
In both places the work came down to the same things: knowing the applicable rules, preparing documents carefully, and seeing how cases actually unfold in the courtroom and in mediation.
items.task: As a Legal Research Intern at Bapas (June–July 2024) and later as Legal Staff at HHL Associates (February–July 2025), I researched the law, helped prepare case documents and attended hearings and mediation sessions.

steps.title: Research the regulations
steps.description: Researched criminal justice and correctional regulations at Bapas Surabaya, and the rules on tort and breach of contract for civil cases at HHL.

steps.title: Draft the pleadings
steps.description: At HHL Associates, prepared drafts of lawsuits, replik and duplik for the supervising attorneys to review.

steps.title: Attend hearings and mediation
steps.description: Attended tort (PMH), breach of contract (wanprestasi) and marriage case hearings, and mediation sessions, including at Pengadilan Negeri Malang Kelas IA.

steps.title: Record and follow up
steps.description: Noted what happened at each session and the next steps for the case file.

items.title: Employee Engagement and KPI Monitoring for 90 People
items.role: Manager, Human Resources Employees and Relations
items.summary: Introduced KPI monitoring and a 360° feedback system for 90 employees, and was named Manager of the Month (May 2025) with a 95% KPI score.
situation: PT. Kunci Hukum was growing quickly, and performance was still judged informally. Managers had no shared view of productivity, and feedback mostly travelled in one direction, from the top down.
Attendance, overtime and engagement activities were tracked in separate files, which made it hard to see patterns or to recognise strong contributors consistently.
items.task: I started as HR staff and became Manager of the HR Employees and Relations division. I was responsible for building a fairer way to measure performance and for keeping engagement programmes running for 90 employees.

steps.title: KPI and 360° feedback
steps.description: Worked with team leads to define KPIs per role and rolled out a 360° feedback process so evaluation also reflected peers and direct reports.

steps.title: Monthly appraisal
steps.description: Ran a monthly appraisal cycle, backed by spreadsheet-based attendance and overtime records.

steps.title: Onboarding and offboarding
steps.description: Handled onboarding for new staff and offboarding for those leaving the company.

steps.title: Peer counselling
steps.description: Set up peer counselling so staff had a colleague to talk to about work concerns.

steps.title: Awarding
steps.description: Ran staff recognition and awards, alongside team bonding activities, and documented each event for the HR report.

resultNotes: Recognised as Best Staff, Human Resources, and later as Manager of the Month (May 2025).
The division was named Best Performing Division and Best Division for HR Employee Engagement and Relations.

items.title: Legal Research and Publications: Derivative Suits, Predatory Pricing and Judicial Review
items.summary: Wrote a comparative study of derivative suits in Indonesia, Japan and Singapore, and co-authored two published journal articles.
situation: Corporate law gives shareholders a derivative suit to act on the company's behalf when its own directors will not. How well that mechanism works in practice differs a great deal between legal systems.
Alongside that study, two research projects looked at competition law in e-commerce and at how well the public understands judicial review at the Constitutional Court.
items.task: I was the lead author of the derivative suit study and a co-author of the two journal articles.

steps.title: Derivative suits as corporate oversight
steps.description: Analysed how effective derivative suits are as a corporate oversight mechanism in Indonesia, compared with Japan and Singapore.

steps.title: Predatory pricing in e-commerce
steps.description: Co-authored a case study of predatory pricing on the Lazada platform, published in the Indonesian Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities (December 2024).

steps.title: Public understanding of judicial review
steps.description: Co-authored a study of how the public understands the object, subject and timing of judicial review at the Constitutional Court, published in Veteran Society: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat, Vol. 6 No. 2 (2025).

resultNotes: Analisis Praktek Predatory Pricing dalam E-Commerce (Studi Kasus Platform Lazada), Indonesian Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities, 2024.
Analisis Pemahaman Masyarakat Terkait Objek, Subjek dan Waktu dalam Pengujian Undang-Undang ke Mahkamah Konstitusi, Veteran Society: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat, Vol. 6 No. 2, 2025.

items.title: Class of Insight: a National Webinar with a KPK Speaker
items.team: Web Development, Content and Event Organization divisions
items.summary: Planned and delivered Class of Insight featuring Edi Suryanto (KPK), coordinating three divisions to reach 125% of the participant target.
situation: Forlawtous.id runs educational and human capital development programs for law students and young professionals. Its flagship events depended on three separate divisions (Web Development, Content and Event Organization) that each worked to their own calendar.

Class of Insight was planned as the community's most visible event to date, with a speaker from the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK). Registration, promotion and the programme itself all had to line up inside a fixed timeline and budget.
items.task: As Director Project Management, I was responsible for the plan end to end: timeline, budget, cross-division coordination and the final run of the event.
items.quote: A good event is mostly decided before the day itself. Clear owners and honest deadlines did more for us than any last-minute push.

steps.title: Scope and timeline
steps.description: Set the event goals, a registration target and a working timeline, then agreed milestones with each division lead.

steps.title: Budget and speaker
steps.description: Prepared the budget, confirmed the speaker and aligned the session topic with the audience we wanted to reach.

steps.title: Weekly coordination
steps.description: Ran a short weekly check-in across Web, Content and Event teams so registration pages, promotion and logistics stayed in step.

steps.title: Event day and review
steps.description: Directed the run of show on the day and closed with a written evaluation for the next committee.

resultNotes: Registrations passed the target, closing at 125% of what the committee had planned for.
The three-division workflow was documented and reused for later programmes.

items.title: Launching the Official Forlawtous.id Website
items.summary: Led the planning and launch of the organisation's official website, working with the Web Development and Content divisions.
situation: Forlawtous.id had been publishing its educational content and event information through social media alone. Visitors had no single place to find the programmes, the team or the articles.
A website would need developers, writers and the events team to work from the same plan, and the launch had to be ready before the next programme cycle.
items.task: As Director Project Management, I owned the delivery plan, the schedule and the coordination between the divisions that would build and fill the site.

steps.title: Define the scope
steps.description: Agreed on the pages, features and priorities for the first release with the Web Development and Content leads.

steps.title: Plan the build
steps.description: Broke the work into milestones with owners and dates, and tracked the budget alongside them.

steps.title: Prepare the content
steps.description: Coordinated writers and the events team so every page had approved copy before the site went live.

steps.title: Launch and hand over
steps.description: Went live on schedule and documented how the site would be maintained by the next committee.

resultNotes: The organisation now has an official home for its programmes and articles.
Maintenance steps were handed over in writing.
